newsitem.title: USA: TVA to seek ways to pay for water services.
newsitem.headline: TVA to seek ways to pay for water services.

text.p: The Tennessee Valley Authority is going to develop a plan to pay for water protection services that the federal government currently funds for TVA, according to the Clinton administration's budget proposal released Thursday.

President Clinton proposed to provide $106 million in the 1998 fiscal year, the same as in 1997, to maintain navigable channels, control floods, develop technology, and run community programs related to TVA.
"The Budget also announces TVA's intention to develop a plan that would eliminate Federal government funding for these programs for TVA for 1999 and beyond," the White House budget request said.

"During 1997 and 1998, TVA will work with Congress, State and local governments and other interested parties and will undertake a major effort to find alternate ways to fund, organize and manage these programs," the proposal said.
The move, proposed by TVA, is in preparation for the opening of power markets to competition, TVA chairman Craven Crowell said at a news conference Thursday in Knoxville.

"The proposal for TVA to end all federal funding for its appropriated programs is important to TVA's power system," he said. "It supports the administration initiatives to ... balance the budget, and it removes the misimpression that TVA power is subsidized."
TVA is a government-owned corporation which covers the costs of its power business through its rates.
